Now viewing one reference from each of 4 different classes:

The Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus reference (Bugwood_1568049) looks extremely similar to the test image (1568051) — consecutive Bugwood IDs, same field setting, same leaf distortion pattern. Let me check 2 more classes to complete the 4-class requirement.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image (Bugwood 1568051)**: Shows severe leaf curling/twisting, distorted growing tips, crinkled/shoestring leaf deformation, and some small necrotic spots — classic viral mosaic symptoms on tomato.
- **Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus ref (Bugwood 1568049)**: Near-identical appearance — same twisted/distorted leaves, same growing tip deformation, consecutive Bugwood IDs (strongly suggesting same disease photo series).
- **TSWV ref**: Shows more advanced whole-plant collapse with dark bronzing necrosis — different pattern.
- **Bacterial_Wilt**: Vascular streaming test — clearly different.
- **Verticillium_Wilt**: Yellowing/bleaching wilting, not the twisting distortion pattern in the test image.

The leaf distortion (filiform/shoestring symptom, curling, crinkling) combined with the consecutive Bugwood ID is conclusive.
